abstract: This paper describes the development and evaluation of a system to calculate temperatures and ratings of HPOF pipe-type cables in real-time. Algorithms applying modern estimation and identification technology to perform these tasks have been designed and demonstrated on two operational cables. Test results give estimates of conductor temperature within ±7% of the actual conductor temperature over a 0°C-125 °C range.

articleTitle: BPA 1100 kV Transmission System Development-Planning, Program, and Objectives
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper summarizes current system planning studies for application of 1100 kV to the Pacific Northwest transmission system, the associated test and development program, and construction of two test lines. It compares 500 and 1100 kV costs and shows 1100 kV to be economical at loadings above 4,000-5,000 MW. The two test lines consist of 1200 kV Lyons Electrical Prototype Line at Lyons, Oregon, and the 1200 kV Moro Mechanical Test Line at Moro, Oregon.

articleTitle: Progress in Self-Commutated Inverters for Fuel Cells and Batteries
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Work has continued on development of large self- commutated inverters1 for commercial fuel cell applications resulting in successful on-line demonstration with a 1 MW fuel cell pilot plant. Predicted performance was achieved with excellent operating characteristics including delivery of leading or lagging vars within the inverter rating. These results are presented herein. In addition, work was initiated under sponsorship of the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI) and the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to adapt this technology to utility energy storage with advanced batteries now under development and intended for use starting in the late 1980's. Reversible operation without polarity switching has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: An Ultrafast Fault Sensor for a Fault Current Limiting Device
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A power system fault current limiting device must act quickly if it is to limit the initial fault current.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation for Determining Step and Touch Potentials Resulting from Faults or Open Neutrals in Urd Cable
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A computer simulation is described which enables the determination of voltages on the surface and within the earth caused by: (1) a phase-to- neutral fault, (2) a fault with simultaneous open neutrals on either side, and (3) an open neutral. The buried cable and associated ground rods are modeled as a set of interconnected cylindrical segments situated in a three-dimensional, two-layered earth model. Simultaneous solution of the interconnected segment circuit and electromagnetostatic equations yields the desired solution. Output from the computer simulation is shown to match closely the data from field tests of faulted cables and other results from the literature. Work supported by EPRI contract RP797-1.

articleTitle: A Decision Methodology for Coal Inventory Optimization
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The procurement of coal as a power plant fuel is formally treated in a decision analysis methodology to assess optimal purchasing and stockpiling strategies. The uncertainties which characterize future prediction of fuel burn, receipt, and market price are expressed in a probabilistic multiperiod inventory model. A dynamic programming optimization procedure of the decision problem is developed. The effects of forecasting uncertainties and price variations are examined in several case studies and the value of perfect information is estimated.

articleTitle: Design and Dynamic Performance of a Steam Turbine Bypass Control System for a Large Fossil-Fired Power Generating Unit
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes the design and the dynamic performance of a novel limited capacity bypass control system proposed for two-shift operation of a 500 MW oil-fired generating unit employing a G.E. turbine. Direct digital controls with analog back-up are applied.

articleTitle: Behavior of Air Insulating GAPS of DC Systems Under Impulse, DC and Composite Voltages
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper deals with the behavior of air insulating gaps of direct current (dc) transmission systems in the voltage range of ±600 kV to ±1 200 kV. The gaps studied were simulating either a bipolar dc tower or a bipolar rigid bus system. The influence of the terminations of the two ends of the insulator supporting the bus was investigated by using a single bus supported at one end. The breakdown voltage of the gaps was determined for a pure impulse, pure dc voltage or composite voltage formed by a dc on which an impulse was superimposed. The proximity effect of one pole on the pole-to-ground breakdown voltage of the other was also investigated.

articleTitle: Impact of Dispersed Supply Management on Electric Distribution Planning and Operations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Small-scale Dispersed Storage and Generation (DSG) technologies connected to the electric distribution system may offer many of the advantages of central supply management options such as pumped-hydro storage and interconnections. In addition, they may provide benefits to the distribution systems by reducing capacity requirements, improving reliability, and lowering losses.

articleTitle: Pole-By-Pole Model of a Linear Induction Machine Using Conformal Mapping Coefficients
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The d,q pole-by-pole model extends the notion of rotating coupled circuits to the analysis of linear induction machines (LIMs). The initial derivation of this model required a lengthening of the primary iron as leading and trailing end effects were better modeled by additional rail poles. This paper shows this lengthening of the primary can have detrimental effects on simulation results, and develops a conformal mapping analysis which uses the actual primary length as leading and trailing effects are modeled. Comparisons to test data show the model with a nonlengthened primary must be used to accurately simulate certain types of LIMs.

articleTitle: Loading of Substation Electrical Equipment with Emphasis on Thermal Capability Part II-Application
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The methodology for establishing thermal loading capability of substation electrical equipment and material should recognize system loading and ambient weather conditions in addition to the unit thermal parameters. Application of a recently developed methodology may show significant potential economic benefits, improved utilization of substation plant investment and satisfactory service performance and equipment maintenance requirements.

articleTitle: BPA 1100 kV Transmission System Development-Environmental Studies
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Environmental studies are an integral part of the Bonneville Power Administration Lyons 1200-kV prototype line test program being conducted at Lyons, Oregon. Through the first two growing seasons following energization, these studies have documented the lack of significant impact of the facility on tree and crop growth, cattle, honeybees and wildlife. Douglas fir trees left growing near the line have experienced some damage due to induced corona which is similar to that documented for EHV lines.

articleTitle: An Efficient State Variable Transmission Line Model
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Lumped models of distributed systems (power transmission lines) are considered. It is shown that models derived by a finite Fourier cosine transform are quite efficient, when compared to conventional pi and tee section models, in that the number of state variables is minimized. This paper is an introduction to the use of distributed system "modes of response" in developing these lumped models for single and multiconductor transmission lines including ground conduction and skin effect.

articleTitle: On the Speed Control of Wound-Rotor Induction Motors Using Rotor Impedance Control
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Significant improvements in the performance of rotor impedance control for constant speed operation of wound-rotor induction motors can be achieved by the introduction of an inductor as a third element of the series resistor-capacitor combination in the rotor circuit. These improvements include better speed regulation and a reduction in physical size of capacitor throughout the speed control range. However, for higher speed ranges the addition of a parallel R-L section is found necessary for further improvement in performance.

articleTitle: Insulation Coordination Designs of HVDC Converter Installations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: There have been as many insulation coordination schemes as there exits HVDC transmission systems throughout the world due to the complexity and variety of terminal arrangements. This paper presents the first consolidated treatise with heretofore needed completeness and a significant amount of previously unpublished data obtained from surveys. It furnishes a comprehensive digest of tried schemes from which new HVDC converter terminals can be designed. Included are equipment insulation levels, arrester protective characteristics, and even protective margins where possible on each of the varied schemes.

articleTitle: Studies on Cooling of Gap-Pickup Turbogenerator Rotors with Cross-Flow Ventilation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The total pressure difference developed by gap pickup rotors is studied by defining the velocity distribution in the gap of rough surfaces. A theoretical eauation is derived for determining its value.

articleTitle: Impacts of Electric Heat on Generation and Primary Fuel Requirements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Electric utilities are forecasting increased penetrations of electric heat as a result of potential shortages and higher prices of heating oil and natural gas. However, the amount, the type, and the insulation levels of the electric heated structures, and thus the resulting benefits and implications remain uncertain. A credible evaluation of electric heat benefits and implications requires an aggregate evaluation of generating capacity and electric demand over a realistic planning period. Methods for performing these evaluations have been developed by Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute. These methods couple a physically and weather based electric demand forecast model with a generation planning model that utilizes linear programming to calculate the corresponding optimal generation and operating strategy. This data is then postprocessed to calculate the incremental generation and primary fuel requirements for electric heat. This paper employs a New York State data base of electric generation, load patterms, electric heat forecasts and weather to calculate the generation and primary fuel requirements for electric heat during the 1980 to 1999 planning period.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of Load Loss in Shell Form Transformers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes the development of a mathematical model of load loss in shell form power transformers. Theoretical loss calculations are modified by regressing them against test data to obtain estimates of winding eddy loss and stray loss in tanks. While the specific model presented here applies only to shell form transformers, the method used to develop the model is general and can also be applied to core form transformers. The model has led to a greater understanding of load loss and has provided the insight necessary to effectively reduce this loss.

articleTitle: Major Electrical Equipment Proposed for Tidal Power Plants in the Bay of Fundy
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The paper discusses general considerations and future possibilities for the design of generating equipment for tidal power plants with particular reference to Bay of Fundy sites. Factors affecting the design of turbines, generators, excitation system, powerhouse layout and the main electrical connections are reviewed. Various alternatives for transmission of power to shore are listed and the choice of SF6 gas insulated bus duct is substantiated by comparative data. Advantages of integrating the high-voltage switching station with the powerhouse, using SF6 gas insulated metal-clad switchgear are discussed. Application of computers and microprocessors is envisaged. The paper concludes that advances in technology can make a significant contribution to economic development of tidal power.

articleTitle: SF6 Gas Circuit Breaker, New Solution for Generator Main Circuit Switching
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: After a short circuit in a large capacity generator main circuit in power plant, current zero transition may fail to occur for many cycles. The authors show that with a suitably designed SF6 gas circuit breaker arc resistance acts to cause current zero transition, making interruption possible, and further that characteristics of SF6 gas make it eminently suitable for generator breakers having the large current carrying capacity demanded in large power plants and also having the capability for repetitive switching of large load currents, as demanded in pumped storage power plants.

articleTitle: Measurements of RIV on Large EHV Apparatus in High Voltage Laboratory
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: North American practice for the measurement of Radio Interference Voltage, (RIV), on EHV apparatus is specified by the NEMA 107 Standard. The recommended measurement frequency is 1 MHz but at this frequency physically large test circuits do not represent the service condition. The measured levels of RIV for EHV apparatus may be unrealistically high at 1 MHz. This phenomenon is caused by an increase of RIV signals due to an internal resonance in the test circuit. This increased reading cannot be corrected by the application of the Circuit RIV Factor "p" since the circuit responses of the calibration and test set-ups are different.

articleTitle: Studies on Corona Performance of Insulator Assemblies for UHV Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes the results of a series of investigation into corona performance of proto type insulator assemblies for UHV transmission lines. For the shielding rings of UHV insulator assemblies, satisfactory RIV characteristics under wet condition was found not to be obtained by simply extrapolating the design practice of EHV insulator assemblies. By the best use of the shielding function of conductors, if relatively small shielding rings are installed at the energized end of the insulator string, the RIV can be restricted below a target value. The insulator assemblies equipped with such shielding rings showed a satisfactory performance from AN point of view.

articleTitle: Analysis of Experimental Data on the Electric Strength of Long Air Gaps
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of published experimental data used for calculating the electric strength of long air gaps between conductor-ground and conductor-tower, using the "critical-charge" method. The study of actual testing conditions provides a basis for explaining certain discrepancies in the results reported by different authors. The paper concludes that the electric strength of long air gaps increases steadily with their length and that no saturation limit exists.

articleTitle: Behavior of Long Insulator Strings in Dry Conditions
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The behavior of long insulator strings under switching and lightning impulses and AC voltage is studied up to 750 kV. With increasing short-circuit currents, it is necessary to fix the spark between specially designed electrodes in order to preserve other metallic pieces from the thermal effects of the arc.

articleTitle: Automatic Generation Control of Jointly-Owned Generating Units
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A set of procedures and algorithms are developed for automatic generation control of generating units that are jointly-owned by two or more utilities. The control performance is examined using the results of simulation tests. Recommendations are given for future work on improved procedures for coordinated economic dispatch involving jointly-owned generating units.

articleTitle: An Integral Equation Formulation for Electromagnetic Field Analysis in Electrical Apparatus
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: An integral equation formulation is obtained for the solution of electric and magnetic polarization in the material body subjected to external excitations. Numerical treatment of saturable magnetic field problems is facilitated by the introduction of a function called 'co-reluctivity' to describe the property of the magnetic material. The Gauss-Seidel iterative procedure is applied for solving the resulting system of nonlinear algebraic equations in order to overcome extremely large memory requirements in a three -dimensional problem by means of magnetic tape or disc operations.

articleTitle: Protection of Auxiliary Power Systems in a Nuclear Power Plant
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper outlines the electrical protection for the 4.16 kV and 480 V auxiliary power systems in a nuclear power plant. The paper describes the protection philosophy, selection of protective devices, and the bases of their coordination and settings.

articleTitle: Time Constants of Unsymmetrical Short Circuits of Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Unsymmetrical short circuits of alternators are governed by periodic coefficient differential linear equations. The exact form of the solution is established on a rigorous mathematical basis. It is shown that time constants may vary very strongly when frequency decreases.

articleTitle: Loading of Substation Electrical Equipment with Emphasis on Thermal Capability Part I-Principles
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Nameplate ratings for substation equipment do not always represent the maximum loading capability of the equipment because they do not reflect the influence of the environmental factors and loading patterns which will exist when the equipment is ultimately placed in service. This paper discusses the principles of thermal capability and describes the environmental factors and loading patterns which influence the maximum loading capability of substation equipment. A companion paper, Part II, describes the application of these principles and factors in determining the thermal capability of specific substation equipment.

articleTitle: Four-Terminal Impedance Current Transformer Bridge with Resistive Ratio Arm
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The most widely used ratio transformer bridge techniques available for comparing four-terminal impedances are reviewed.

articleTitle: The Accuracy of Statistical Methods in Evaluating the Insulation of EHV Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The insulation of a 400 KV transmission line as far as switching overvoltages are concerned has been evaluated through the probabilistic approach. The statistical data of switching overvoltages have been obtained by means of one thousand line reclosing operations simulated through an appropriate computer program The switching tests have been grouped to study the influence of the statistical pattern. The risk of failure as calculated by means of three approved statistic al diagrams has overlapping regions resulting in low- reliability insulation values. To increase the reliability of the results it looks necessary that some relevant universal criteria should be specified.

articleTitle: Selection of Design Features for 737 and 823 MVA Hydrogenerators for Itaipu Project
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The unprecedented capacity of the ITAIPU hydroelectric station and the size of its generating units made it imperative to reappraise the nature of the problems associated with the design and fabrication of giant size hydroelectric machinery.

articleTitle: Cross-Field Analysis of Asymmetric Three-Phase Induction Motors Extensions to Single- and Two-Phase Machines Thereof
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The cross-field theory as applied to single-phase induction motors is extended to develop a concise yet comprehensive theory for asymmetric three-phase induction motors. Each phase is represented by its equivalent circuit not only to allow for uneven direct transformer interactions due to asymmetric locactions of phase windings but also to account for the different number of turns, wire size, winding factor, etc., each phase may have. The accuracy of the theory was confirmed by actual measurements on symmetric and asymmetric three-phase induction motors. Computed and test data on some motors are included for illustration. It is also shown that the general three-phase development can be easily applied to determine the behavior of two- and single-phase induction machines-a useful feature for unified computer-aided design - by eliminating one and two phase windings respectively. Not only the procedural details for determining the performance of single-and two-phase induction motors are given but comparisons of numerical and test results on some output entities are included as well.

articleTitle: Control of Large Power Systems Based on Situation Recognition and High Speed Simulation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The operation of large power systems places an increasing importance on the security of the system which must be evaluated in steady state, transient, and long term dynamic situations. A method based on "situation recognition" and high speed simulation for on-line security computations is proposed and analyzed. The method combines the advantages of high speed hybrid computer simulation and pattern recognition methods, and, at the same time, has the flexibility of a pure digital simulation.

articleTitle: Simplified Analysis of Rectangular Grounding Grids
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A simple and rapid method for designing and analyzing regular, multimeshed rectangular grounding grids is presented. The procedure is based on an extension of principles enunciated in IEEE Standard 80 dated June 30, 1976. By this method, using an engineering type pocket calculator, touch potentials can be determined in a few minutes for any given set of dimensions, resistivity, and fault current.

articleTitle: Fundamentals of Fusing to Minimize Case Rupture in Distribution Capacitor Banks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of capacitor-case rupture in pole-mounted distribution capacitor banks.. Fundamentals of fusing to minimize capacitor-case rupture are discussed. Also considered is the exposure to nuisance melting as a result of inrush currents.

articleTitle: Breakdown Characteristics for a Heated Busbar in a Gas-Filled Duct
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Breakdown was studied for a 50 mm gap between concentric cylinders at a pressure of 1 atmosphere. The inner cylinder was heated up to 120°C with the outer cylinder at 20°C. Heating caused the alternating and switching impulse breakdown voltages of SF to fall by about 15%; with the inner cylinder at 40°C, the fall was 7%. With the inner cylinder positive and without heating, spark conditioning caused the direct breakdown voltage in nitrogen to increase greatly and the scatter to fall sharply; conditioning was much less effective for negative polarity. The alternating breakdown voltages of SF6 and nitrogen fell slightly with conditioning.

articleTitle: Determination of Lightning Current Using Frame Aerials
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A method of measurement of magnetic fields due to lightning discharges using frame aerials has been developed, and a corresponding model to determine its current magnitude is Presented. Comparisons of results of magnitudes and rates of rise of lightning currents thus obtained show good general agreement with previous results, particularly from tropical areas.

articleTitle: An Integrated Information System for Power Planning Studies -SIIPEP-
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The Integrated Information System for Power Planning Studies -SIIPEP- is an interactive Data Base that automatically Prepares information for Power System Planning models, reducing manual data handling when updating certain Parameters that are representative of a studs case. Information retrieval from SIIPEP to user application is realized in a simple was by a user interface that avoids modifications to existing models. This interface is supported by SIIPEP functions. This Paper describes the results and experiences of the first stage of its design and Presents the theoretical basis for the second stage.

articleTitle: Multiobjective Load Management Techniques for Electrified Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper develops a methodology for managing electric-train-loads through the adjustment of their trajectories in the 3-dimensional space of speed, time and distance. The management process involves reconciling two conflicting objectives-the total energy, W, and the total time, T, required to complete each journey. A multiobjective approach is used. For a given hardware configuration, the approach generates a continuous curve (the "noninferior surface") that represents the best posible tradeoffs between W and T. By staying on this curve one can achieve energy savings with the least possible increase in T, and vice versa.

articleTitle: Transmission Lines - Effect of Earth Resistivity on Magnetic Field, Images and Equivalent Circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: An analytical method is described to account for the effect of earth resistivity on the magnetic and electric field intensities near transmission lines. The effect is derived from the boundary conditions at the airearth surface. The field intensity vectors, even for a single-conductor line, trace elipses at any point in the transversal plane in space. Fields are calculated for frequencies, l0kHz to 1000 kHz and earth resistivit ties 20 Ω-m to 2000 Ω-m. It is shown that no concept of image current can be realized.

articleTitle: New Dual-Element Current-Limiting Power Fuse with Full Protection Capability Against any Fault Current
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A newly developed current-limiting fuse , called the universal fuse , has dual fuse-elements connected in series: one is made of gold-silicon alloy with a low melting point and covered with polytetrafluorethylene arc-extinguishing tube , and the other is an ordinary ribbon-like silver element . The gold alloy element performs for low-current interruption , and the silver one , principally for high-current interruption . This fuse can be applied for reliable protection against a full-range fault current from a minimum fusing current to a heavy short-circuit fault current . It has such practically excellent properties as low temperature rise , high reliability against short-time and long-term deteriorations , and feasible protection co-ordination.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Heuristic Synthesis Methods for Electricity Transmission Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper discusses and compares several synthesis methods for electricity distribution networks, assessing the validity of the feasibility constraints used in the various methods. Established methods, together with some original ideas, are explained; special reference is made to heuristics based on group-transfer concepts. The algorithms have been applied to data extracted from case studies to simulate a green-field synthesis of network configuration, thus results are comparable with existing network configurations. The results were produced using an interactive computing system.

articleTitle: Power System Planning Practice in Italy
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A brief description is given of the main characteristics (load, generation and transmission) of the Italian Electric Power System of today and in the relatively near future (1985), together with an indication of its possible long term (1985-2000) development.

articleTitle: Development of 500 kV Submarine O.F. Cable
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This report describes the development results of a 500 kV submarine O.F. cable and factory joint. We manufactured a 500 kV submarine O.F. cable (1 x 1300mm2) on trial and confirmed that it can be used in practical applications. As to the factory joint which is indispensable to the long-distance submarine cable, we succeeded in developing a factory joint having the electrical and mechanical characteristics equivalent to those of the 500 kV submarine O.F. cable and confirmed that the large-capacity long-distance submarine cable can be put into practical use.

articleTitle: Magnetohydrodynamic Power Generation: Program Planning and Status
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper is concerned with the phased development of the MHD power system program and the development issues which are being addressed. System engineering considerations for the development logic and design criteria are established in terms of systems-emphasizing open cycle MHD-and components - combustor, generator, materials, seed recovery, emission control, magnets and power conversion systems.

articleTitle: Development of a DC Linear Motor (II) Research for a Ground Coil and a Field-Magnet
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: We have constructed a test facility for the linear motor car mainly to examine its propulsion characteristics. The 3.3 ton vehicle has a 2 ton propulsion force and can be accelerated to 165 Km/h in 200 m. In this paper, our investigation of the field-magnet and armature coils on the ground is reported. We discuss the correspondence of our theoretical analysis with the results of experiments. We believe that the results of our investigation can be readily applied to an actural DCLM line.

articleTitle: Surge Response Characteristics of HV Pipe-Type Cable from Field Tests
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The unavailability of high-voltage pipe- type cable for impulse propagation tests has hindered the development of creditable models for si'mulation studies. Low-voltage field tests have been conducted on a 13.9 km9 230 kV cable and subsequent analysis has substantiated the approach as a valid method for obtaining the desired high-voltage surge response characteristics without any risk to the cable. The results obtained, then, from low-voltage tests can be reliably used as a check for simulation studies.

articleTitle: DC and AC Thermal Stability of Oil Impregnated Paper
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Operating conditions which can lead a dc stressed oil impregnated paper, insulation to thermalinstability are analyzed. A computing method is developed for this purpose. Tests both on plane models and on cable samples verify the computed behaviour.

articleTitle: The Freezing Method for the Oil Stop in POF Cable Repair
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A freeze chamber making effective use of Joule Thomson effect and a sub-chamber were developed to establish a freezing method for oil stop of POF cable.

articleTitle: Flashovers Across Porcelain-Clad Circuit Breakers Due to Atmospheric Contamination
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Atmospheric contamination flashovers can occur across porcelain-clad circuit breakers either during normal opening operations or while in the open position. Such external flashovers across a breaker pole can result either in damaging the breaker or reestablishing the previous fault or establishing a new fault in which the breaker is helpless to clear. Three cited cases, each occurring on different types of circuit breakers with different voltage ratings, are presented for the first time. Some of the fundamental principles that lead to atmospheric contamination flashovers on porcelain insulator surfaces also are presented. The purpose of the paper is to alert the power industry to the possibility of such flashovers, to present an analysis of the problem, and to suggest practices and corrective measures to minimize such occurrences.

articleTitle: Modeling Experiments Applied to Ceramic Air-Magnetic ARC Chutes
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Modeling experiments applied to ceramic air-magnetic arc chutes have been developed and studied. These tests were conducted using a synthetic capacitor bank and a simplified model which contained all the arc chute parameters but did not contain moving contacts. The experiments concentrated on the following parameters: Magnetic field, plate spacing, plate geometry, and the ceramic plate material. These experiments demonstrate that modeling techniques can be effectively used on air-magnetic arc chutes to quickly evaluate a large variety of design variations.

articleTitle: Control Criteria and Practices Related to Capacity Emergencies
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper is one of a series prepared by the Current Operational Problems (COPs) Working Group with the goal of focusing the attention of the industry on high priority problems faced by those who are involved in the actual operation of power systems.

articleTitle: Electrical Design and Steady State Performance of Generrex * Excitation Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a description of the steady-state electrical performance objectives of the new GENERREX* excitation system now being applied to large steam turbine-generators. Some of the considerations entering into the proper selection of the design characteristics for the various components are also discussed. Analytical performance predictions are compared to test results obtained during on-site operation of a generator unit with the prototype GEERREX excitation system.

articleTitle: Accounting for Intangibles in a Present Worth Comparison of Advanced Power Generation Alternatives
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A methodology is described which considers both tangible and intangible attributes of advanced electric power generation cycles. It enables an assessment to be made of the costs and benefits to be derived from developing each of the cycles.

articleTitle: Application of the Minimum Revenue Requirement - Investment Opportunity Theory to Economic Evaluations with Complex Cash Flows
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Application of the Minimum Revenue Requirement - Investment Opportunity Return (MRR-IOR) Method1 for performing economic comparisons of alternatives in a regulated utility environment is presented in this paper. The procedure for establishing the Investment Opportunity Return (IOR) criterion available to a regulated utility is illustrated, and the methodology for applying the MRR-IOR theory to complex cash flow problems in which capital investments occur over a number of years is presented. The distinction is made between evaluating essential projects and nonessential or efficiency type projects, with detailed examples of both types of evaluations being given in the paper. The use of sensitivity and risk analyses in performing economic evaluations is also documented.

articleTitle: Foyers Pumped Storage Scheme
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The Foyers Pumped Storage Project, commissioned in 1974, is the third major pumped storage scheme in the United Kingdom (UK), the second using reversible pump turbines and the first using shaft-type station construction. The paper briefly describes the station layout and plant and the various modes of operation and outlines the pump starting methods considered at the planning stage. A full description is given of the variable freauency static convertor method of pump starting adopted. The paper also describes in some detail operational experience associated with the electrical and mechanical plant since commissioning.

articleTitle: Design Considerations in the Development of a New Ground Distance Relay
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The combined effects of fault resistance and load flow cause the apparent impedance for ground faults to vary over a wide range. A new ground distance relay using a four input phase comparator provides improved security with a fault resistance capability similar to that of a simple quadrature polarized ground distance relay.

articleTitle: The Impact of Alternate Energy Resources on the Future Supply of Electric Power
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In the remaining years of this century, the electricity sector will experience two fundamental developments: (1) the demand for electricity will far exceed the demand for other forms of energy, and (2) the resource base for electricity generation will change dramatically as we use less oil and natural gas and turn to coal and uranium. Increased reliance on coal and uranium will pose a number of technological and nontechnological problems. The nontechnological problems turn out to be the most difficult, and the future supply of electricity will in large part depend on their resolution.

articleTitle: 1979 Index IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This index covers all technical items - papers, correspondence, reviews, etc. - that appeared in this periodical during the year, and items from previous years that were commented upon or corrected in this year. Departments and other items may also be covered if they have been judged to have archival value. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item, listed under the first author's name. The primary entry includes the coauthors' names, the title of the paper or other item, and its location, specified by the publication abbreviation, year, month, and inclusive pagination. The Subject Index contains entries describing the item under all appropriate subject headings, plus the first author's name, the publication abbreviation, month, and year, and inclusive pages. Note that the item title is found only under the primary entry in the Author Index.
